claim: All property shall be valued at its market value.
Local board of appeal and equalization meetings must be held between April 1 and May 31 each year.

A person who fails to appear before the local board after notice of an assessment increase, or fails to apply for review, may not appear before the county board of appeal and equalization (with exceptions, e.g. no notice of market value at least five days before the local meeting).

A property tax petition to district court or Tax Court is served on the county auditor, and the petition and proof of service must be filed with the district court administrator on or before April 30 of the year the tax becomes payable.

If notice of a valuation, classification or exempt-status change is first given after February 28 of the year taxes are payable, the petitioner has 60 days from the mailing date of the notice to appeal.
Appeal of a commissioner of revenue order to Tax Court must be served and filed within 60 days after the notice date of the order; the Tax Court may extend up to 30 more days for cause.
Tax Court Small Claims Division appeal fee is $150.

State deed tax is imposed on each deed or instrument conveying real property in Minnesota, applied to net consideration.
Deed tax is $1.65 when there is no consideration or consideration is $3,000 or less (and for mergers/designated transfers).
When consideration exceeds $3,000, deed tax is .0033 (0.33%) of net consideration, exclusive of liens or encumbrances remaining at sale.
Deed tax is due when the taxable deed is presented for recording.
Deed tax proceeds are apportioned 97% to the state general fund and 3% to the county revenue fund.

Exempt from deed tax: deed of distribution by a personal representative, sheriff's/referee's certificate of sale in foreclosure, certificates of redemption, marriage dissolution decree transfers, partition deeds between co-owners, transfer on death deeds, executory contracts, mortgages, and leases.
When real estate is sold for more than $3,000, the grantor, grantee or their agent must file a certificate of real estate value with the county auditor when the deed is presented for recording.

Foreclosure by advertisement requires a default that makes the power of sale operative, no pending action on the debt, and recorded mortgage and assignments.
Six weeks' published notice of sale is required, and a copy must be served like a summons at least four weeks before the sale on the person in possession if the premises are occupied.
The mortgagor generally has six months after the sale to redeem by paying the sale price plus interest at the mortgage rate (6% if none stated) and other permitted sums.
A 12-month redemption period applies in specified cases, e.g. premises over 40 acres at mortgage execution, certain 10-40 acre agricultural premises, or reverse mortgages.
The foreclosing party may postpone the sale;.
UNCONFIRMED: Minnesota also allows judicial foreclosure under chapter 581; not opened.
The sale is made by the sheriff or deputy at public venue to the highest bidder, in the county where the premises (or part) lie, between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.
The foreclosing party may postpone the sale; no notice of postponement need be published.
A sheriff's or referee's certificate of sale in a mortgage or lien foreclosure sale is exempt from state deed tax.

The mortgagor may redeem within six months after sale (12 months in listed cases); the sheriff may accept a lesser sum if the certificate holder agrees in writing before the redemption period expires.

Small estate affidavit (personal property): 30 days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $75,000 and no personal representative application is pending.

A personal representative may sell, mortgage or lease estate real property, including the homestead, without consent of devisees or heirs unless specifically devised, but the homestead cannot be sold if the spouse takes an interest without the spouse's written consent.
A deed of distribution by a personal representative is exempt from state deed tax.
Seller disclosure requirements do not apply to a transfer to heirs or devisees of a decedent.
